purpose: Target-specific, machine-governed dispositions for container-image vulnerability findings. Replaces the bare global .trivyignore, whose entries were CVE IDs with prose governance: a bare ID suppresses that CVE EVERYWHERE, in every image and every package, so it could silently hide a genuinely new occurrence of the same CVE in a different component.
enforcement_model: The gate scans with NO suppression (--ignorefile /dev/null) to obtain the complete finding set of EVERY platform child it scans, then reconciles that set against the records below. Trivy's own ignore mechanism is never relied upon, so suppression cannot happen without a matching governed record. A record must match EVERY consequence-relevant field of a finding -- advisory id, exact configured image digest, the platform of the child the finding came from, package name, canonical PURL, installed version, severity and result target. Reconciliation is PER PLATFORM: a record governs only findings from the child it names, and the same rules apply to each platform separately -- an unmatched finding fails the gate, and a record that matches nothing fails the gate as unused. A record naming a platform this gate does not scan fails too, because a record that was never given the chance to match is neither satisfied nor stale, and an unscanned platform must not become somewhere to park a disposition beyond review.
severity_policy: `severities` is an explicit governed array of the exact severities the record covers. Ambiguous composites such as HIGH_AND_CRITICAL are rejected: a record approved for HIGH must not silently absorb a CRITICAL that appears later under the same advisory id.
